newsitem.title: FRANCE: What French truckers won in 12-day strike.
newsitem.headline: What French truckers won in 12-day strike.

text.p: French truckers signed a series of accords with employers on the 12th day of a strike blockading the nation's roads and fuel supplies on Friday, although loose ends remain over pay and work time.
The following are details of the five deals, signed by all unions except the Communist-led CGT, and of the proposals to resolve the other issues:

1) Retirement age will be cut to 55 years from 60 for drivers with 25 years service who will take so-called "end of career leave". From 57.5 years, the state will help fund the benefits while employers' payroll charges will be cut.
2) France will ban all trucks from roads on Sundays. Until now, the ban has covered French truck drivers but not foreign truckers. French hauliers had complained of unfair competition.
3) The number of unpaid days of sick leave before truckers are entitled to sick pay will be cut to five from 10.
4) Drivers will be paid expenses for nights away from home regardless of whether they sleep in their cabins or at a hotel.
5) Truckers to get improved union rights, with a cash fund to strengthen organisation.
Pay issues yet to be resolved:
-- The government has promised to issue a decree to impose payment for all hours worked if the two sides fail to agree a deal defining working time within two weeks.

Drivers say they are not paid for dozens of hours a month spent loading and unloading their trucks, for time spent on standby and for compulsory rest breaks. They say payment for such hours would be the equivalent of a 10 percent wage rise.
-- Employers also offered a special 3,000 franc ($600) bonus to be paid in up to three instalments by the end of March 1997, with at least half paid this year.
